stem: Which of the following is chosen in India through an indirect election?
options: Members of the Lok Sabha
The President of India
Members of a Vidhan Sabha
Members of a gram panchayat
explanation: Correct option: (B). The President, the Vice President and members of the Rajya Sabha are elected indirectly by elected representatives. Members of the Lok Sabha, the Vidhan Sabhas and local bodies such as panchayats are elected directly by the citizens.

stem: A class representative chosen in Grade 8 wants to continue in Grade 9 without facing a fresh election. Why is this against democratic principles?
options: Periodic polls keep representatives answerable
Only teachers may choose class representatives
A representative can never be elected twice
A second term always needs a two-thirds vote
explanation: Correct option: (A). Representatives must seek a fresh mandate at regular intervals so that voters can hold them accountable. Re-election is allowed, teachers do not replace voters in a democratic choice, and no special two-thirds rule applies.

stem:
Assertion (A): An election in which only one political party is allowed to contest cannot be called a democratic election.
Reason (R): Voters must have a meaningful choice between alternatives for an election to express their will.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Both statements are true. A one-party contest gives voters no real choice, and it is precisely the absence of meaningful alternatives (stated in R) that makes such an election undemocratic, so R correctly explains A.

stem: Consider: (i) members of the Rajya Sabha, (ii) members of the Lok Sabha, (iii) the Vice President, (iv) members of a municipal corporation. In which of these do citizens vote directly for the person who holds the office?
options: (i) and (iii) only

explanation: Correct option: (D). Lok Sabha members and members of local bodies such as municipal corporations are elected directly by citizens. stem: Members of the Lok Sabha and the Vidhan Sabhas are elected using which electoral system?
options: Proportional representation
First-Past-The-Post system
Two-round majority system
Single transferable vote
explanation: Correct option: (B). The framers of the Constitution chose the plurality or FPTP system for the Lok Sabha and the Vidhan Sabhas. Proportional representation by single transferable vote is used for the Rajya Sabha, the Vidhan Parishad, the President and the Vice President; India does not use a two-round majority system.

stem: In a proportional representation system, voters generally vote for
options: one candidate who must cross 50 per cent
the candidate with the most votes locally
a party, and seats follow its vote share
two leading candidates in a second round
explanation: Correct option: (C). Under proportional representation, people vote for a party and seats are allotted in proportion to each party's share of votes. Needing over 50 per cent and a second round describe the majority system, and the most-votes rule describes FPTP.

stem: In a Lok Sabha constituency, candidates P, Q, R and S receive 34%, 30%, 21% and 15% of the votes respectively. What is the result?
options: P wins, having the most votes
P and Q face a second round
No one wins, as none has 50%
The seat is shared by P and Q
explanation: Correct option: (A). Under FPTP the candidate with the most votes wins even with less than 50 per cent of the votes polled. A second round is a feature of the majority system, and seats are not shared among candidates in a single-member constituency.

stem: A country uses the two-round majority system. In round one, Party X gets 45%, Party Y 40% and Party Z 15%. What happens next?

explanation: Correct option: (D). In the majority system a candidate needs more than 50 per cent; if no one gets it, the top two contest again. stem: In a Vidhan Parishad election by single transferable vote, 3 seats are to be filled and 400 valid votes are cast. What is the quota (minimum votes needed to win)?
explanation: Correct option: (B). Quota = Total valid votes / (Seats to be filled + 1) + 1 = 400 / (3 + 1) + 1 = 100 + 1 = 101. The value 100 forgets the final +1, 134 wrongly divides by 3, and 201 divides by 2 as if only one seat were being filled.

stem:
Assertion (A): Without periodic delimitation, one Member of Parliament may come to represent far more people than another.
Reason (R): The boundaries of parliamentary constituencies are permanently fixed by the Constitution.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

stem: The main aim of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is to
options: redraw constituency boundaries after a population shift

allot election symbols to recognised state parties

explanation: Correct option: (D). SIR updates, verifies and corrects electoral rolls so that no eligible citizen is left out and no ineligible person is included. Redrawing boundaries is delimitation, and registering parties and allotting symbols are separate ECI functions.

stem: During a revision of rolls, officials find a voter enrolled in two constituencies, a voter who has died, and a citizen who has just turned 18 but is not enrolled. What should the revision do?
options: Keep both duplicates; remove the dead voter; add the youth
Remove the duplicate and the dead voter; add the youth
Remove the duplicate; keep the dead voter; add the youth
Remove the duplicate and the dead voter; skip the youth
explanation: Correct option: (B). SIR deletes names for death, change of residence, duplicate enrolment or being permanently untraceable, and adds eligible voters, especially those who have just turned 18. Keeping a duplicate or a dead voter's name would allow misuse, and leaving out the new voter would deny an eligible citizen the vote.

stem: A party secures 7% of the valid votes and wins 2 seats in a State Legislative Assembly election. According to the ECI criteria, it
options: qualifies as a national party at once
stays unrecognised as it needs 8 per cent
qualifies as a state party in that state

stem: Party Q is recognised as a state party in four states. Party R polled over 6% of valid votes in three states in a Lok Sabha election and won four Lok Sabha seats. Which statement is correct?
options: Both Q and R qualify as national parties
Only Q qualifies as a national party

explanation: Correct option: (B). Recognition as a state party in at least four states is enough for national party status, so Q qualifies.
